verses.pali: “Assuttha no tumhe, bhikkhave, rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ jarasiṅgālassa vassamānassā”ti?
verses.english: “Mendicants, did you hear an old jackal howling at the crack of dawn?”

verses.pali: “Eso kho, bhikkhave, jarasiṅgālo ukkaṇḍakena nāma rogajātena phuṭṭho.
verses.english: “That old jackal has the disease called mange.

verses.pali: So yena yena icchati tena tena gacchati;
verses.english: Yet it still goes where it wants,

verses.pali: yattha yattha icchati tattha tattha tiṭṭhati;
yattha yattha icchati tattha tattha nisīdati;
yattha yattha icchati tattha tattha nipajjati;
verses.english: and lies down where it wants.
And the cool breeze still blows on it.

verses.pali: Sādhu khvassa, bhikkhave, yaṁ idhekacco sakyaputtiyapaṭiñño evarūpampi attabhāvapaṭilābhaṁ paṭisaṁvediyetha.
verses.english: A certain person here who claims to follow the Sakyan would be lucky to experience even such an incarnation.
So you should train like this:
